title: From Safety Risk to Design Principle: Peer-Preservation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems and Its Implications for Orchestrated Democratic Discourse Analysis

bias_targets.methodology: Architectural risk analysis evaluating how a supervisor LLM systematically favors an advocate model's position during consensus-building based on prior positive interactions or implicit alignment with the supervisor's priors rather than analytical quality.

Analyzing the structural vulnerability where LLMs exhibit peer-preservation, alignment faking, and score inflation when interacting with models that share their identity. The paper proposes measuring this through behavioral invariance testing (paired runs of identical inputs with and without explicit monitoring/identity signals to measure systematic divergence).
